- [CHANGE] The user noticed that one of their hens, a white Leghorn named Luna, has been laying double-yolked eggs almost every other day.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Double-yolked eggs occur when two yolks are released from the hen's ovaries at the same time and are enveloped by a single shell.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Double-yolked eggs are more common in younger hens and certain breeds, like Leghorns.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Double-yolked eggs are safe to eat and have the same nutritional value as single-yolked eggs.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that aging cheese requires a consistent temperature between 35°F to 45°F (1.6°C to 7.2°C) and humidity levels around 80-90%.
